sections.content: How many people are "financial managers and directors"?

346,795 people

were counted on the census as "financial managers and directors" in England and Wales in March 2021.

This makes this type of work the eighth most common occupation reported on the census.

Financial managers and directors organise, direct and co-ordinate the financial information of companies, the activities and resources of financial institutions, such as banks and insurance companies, and advise on company financial policy.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 40 to 44 years. Of the whole working population 10.9% were aged 40 to 44 years. For people working as "financial managers and directors", 15.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "financial managers and directors" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "financial managers and directors" included:

  • purchasing managers and directors
  • production managers and directors in mining and energy
  • charitable organisation managers and directors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "financial managers and directors" there were more men than women (56.8% compared with 43.2%).

This means "financial managers and directors" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "corporate managers and directors".

Men made up 56.8% and women made up 43.2% of "financial managers and directors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "financial managers and directors" included:

  • research and development (r&d) managers
  • business and financial project management professionals
  • sales related occupations (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "financial managers and directors" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "financial managers and directors" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "financial managers and directors", 6.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (85.3% compared with 14.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (90.1%) than self-employed (9.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Wandsworth, this is in the same region of London.
